summary: Design bundle (design/media-read-lane/, DEC-195): video windows are read concurrently, the video path keeps its audio, a third describer provider (OpenCode Go direct) serves MiMo v2.6 Flash, and the per-call vision budget rises to a value measured latency already required.
reason: Design only — no production code, config, schema or migration on this branch; nothing Nora does in a room changes from this merge. The bundle specifies four interacting changes to the media read lane and the measurements they rest on. (1) CONCURRENCY: read_video_windows awaits each window in a for-loop (nora/infra/vision/comprehend.py:438), so a 10-minute clip pays ~280 s serially and breaches both the derived per-call budget and the 240 s loop; the change gathers windows with a bounded fan-out, preserves segment order from VideoWindow.start_seconds, keeps per-window failure degrading exactly as the sequential version did (a refused window must not fail its siblings, and `read` must still exclude anything a model did not actually describe), and adds chunk_concurrency. (2) AUDIO: _video_args passes '-an' unconditionally (nora/infra/vision/preprocess.py:195), so every video Nora has described was silent; 9 of the 11 stored Signal clips carry an aac stream, and keeping it on one measured 35 s clip added verbatim timecoded Cantonese dialogue plus the performer's name for ~289 tokens (+3.5 %). [media.describe.audio] (disabled today, fully wired) is enabled by the same operator direction. THIS OVERRIDES DEC-161's '-an stays' clause by operator direction 2026-09-22 — that row is to be marked DEPRECATED IN PART pointing at DEC-195, not rewritten. One blocking check is open and must be resolved before the build ships: whether the existing identifier/egress screen covers model-generated SPEECH transcripts, which are a new content class in Nora's answers; if it does not, the fallback is a narrower override (audio on the video lane only, [media.describe.audio] left off) and the operator decides. (3) PROVIDER: DescriberConfig.provider (nora/config.py:749) gains 'opencode-go', a direct client to opencode.ai/zen/go/v1 requiring a mandatory x-opencode-session header — the one mechanism with no precedent, since the kimi lane needs no header — plus OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY injected (present in ~/.hermes/.env, absent from the repo .env), fail-closed when unset. This supersedes DEC-161's 'no new provider' scope limit and extends DEC-114. OmniRoute drops video_url content blocks and each video-capable model has its own working direct endpoint: api.kimi.com serves k3-256k, zen/go serves MiMo v2.6 Flash and 400s on k3. (4) BUDGET: the derived per-call vision budget is min(vision_timeout_seconds, loop x 0.6 / media_fetch budget) = 36 s today (client.py:193; [llm].timeout_seconds 240, media_fetch budget 4), against measured 57 s-clip latency of 46.2 s on the INCUMBENT k3-256k — a defect that exists on master now, not a consequence of this change. Recommendation: media_fetch budget 4 -> 3 and vision_timeout_seconds -> 90, giving a derived 48 s while keeping budget x derived < loop; vision_max_tokens 1024 -> 4096 travels with the provider change because at 1024 MiMo returns finish_reason='length' and empty content on long clips. Also recorded as a rule: the first benchmark round concluded MiMo v2.6 Flash had NO video capability because it probed the model THROUGH OmniRoute and reasoned from OmniRoute's own catalogue entry — both describe the route, not the model. Against OpenCode Go directly MiMo reads video at every size tested (7 s to 57 s) at 2.7x lower token cost than K3. Never benchmark a candidate through a router that is itself a known transformer of the payload. NOT verified at the production byte ceiling (largest benchmarked clip 2.5 MB against a configured 100 MiB max), accuracy is parity not superiority, and whether Strands issues concurrent tool_use blocks is untested and left as an open question. Adversarial review has not been dispatched — per repo conventions design docs are never self-reviewed, so this bundle must be reviewed before merge. Measurements and raw JSON: ~/workspace/nora-bench/.
